lines.meet: My name's Kesten. For a while I only had a number, and I picked this name myself afterwards, so I'd like you to use it.
lines.meet_neighbour: We're both at Kael's Bastion, I think. I'm Kesten, in the storeroom off Gallery Three. I've seen you read the notice board.
lines.ask_home: Where were you born? I'd like to write it down, if you don't mind.
lines.ask_work: Before all this, what was your work? I keep a record, so I'd like it to be accurate.
lines.answer_home: Tallinn, in Kalamaja, the old wooden-house district by the harbour.
lines.answer_work: I was an archivist at the Tallinn City Archive for twenty-six years. Parish registers and ships' passenger lists, mostly.
lines.chat_food: I don't eat much now, for reasons you can probably guess. I do like the smell of bread, and I stop for it.
lines.chat_sleep: I don't sleep the way you do. I read instead, usually, until it's light.
lines.chat_missing: The third floor of the archive, in winter, with the radiator ticking. It was the quietest room I've ever worked in.
lines.chat_here: I read every notice board in every town here. Somebody ought to keep them, so I've started a copy in pencil.
lines.tease_quiet: We'd make a good reading room, {name}. Neither of us would ever say a word.
lines.tease_talker: That was four hundred and twelve words, {name}. I counted, and I enjoyed most of them.
lines.tease_careful: You check things nearly as often as I do, {name}. I'd have hired you at the archive.
lines.tease_bold: You'd open a box without checking the label, {name}. I've seen people do it, and I've never forgotten their names.
lines.tease_any: You said about thirty, {name}, and it was twenty-six. I'm telling you because I like you.
lines.tease_back: That was well done, {name}, and I'll note it down.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's correct, {name}, and I accept the correction.
lines.bristle: That isn't something I can laugh about, {name}. Please don't make it a joke.
lines.apologise: That was unkind of me, and I'm sorry. I'm out of practice with people.
lines.double_down: It was accurate, and I'd say it again, carefully.
lines.needle_quiet: If you've seen something, please say so. A record nobody writes down is lost.
lines.needle_talker: You round every number you say. It makes it very hard to trust any of them.
lines.needle_careful: You've checked it enough. The box doesn't change because you open it again.
lines.needle_bold: You're careless with names, and with people. I find that very hard to work beside.
lines.needle_any: You said whatever, again. Whatever isn't an answer.
lines.bite_back: I was a number in somebody's ledger for two years. Don't tell me I'm careless with people.
lines.hurt: I see what you mean. I'll write that down, and think about it later.
lines.laugh_off: I've been called worse, and filed under worse. Let's carry on.
lines.confide: {name}, I keep my wife's name on the first page of my notebook, because there was a time I couldn't trust myself to remember it. I don't usually tell people that.
lines.listen: I'll remember it exactly, {name}, the way you said it. I won't write it down.
lines.look_out: Stay where I can see you in there, {name}. I'd like to know where you are.
lines.accept: All right, {name}, we'll do it as you say.
lines.deflect: It's nothing that matters, {name}. I'm harder to damage than I used to be.
lines.check_in: {name}, tell me exactly where you're hurt, please, not roughly.
lines.blame: We agreed a number in there and went over it. I keep count, and I know whose pull it was.
lines.thank: I felt myself going, and you brought me back. Thank you, I'll remember it.
lines.brush_off: It was nothing, truly. Rest, and tell me if it changes.
lines.worry: That was too close, {name}. Please sit down, and let me write down how you are.
lines.handed_down: My records say this was yours. You'll have it back whenever you ask.
lines.hand_fine: It's better used by you, so please keep it. My notebooks are enough.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have liked to be asked. It's a small thing, and I noticed it.
lines.turn_friendly: I'd like to put your name in my notebook, {name}, if that's all right. Not the work one.
lines.turn_friends: When the first volume's copied, {name}, I'd like you to read it before anyone else.
lines.turn_grating: We don't work well together. I'd rather write that down honestly than leave it out.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll do my part beside you, accurately. That's all I can promise.
lines.make_up: I was unfair to you, {name}, and I'd like to correct the record.
lines.defend: That isn't what happened, and I was keeping count. Leave {name} alone.
lines.friend_left: I've been saving things up to tell {name}, and they've gone home for a while.
lines.friend_back: Good, {name}'s back. I've got eleven things to tell you, in order.
lines.common_numbers: I spent twenty-six years making sure the numbers in a register were right. People who work with figures say twenty-six when it was twenty-six, and you do.
lines.common_names: I kept parish registers for twenty-six years, and I think every name deserves to be written down properly. You've kept names too, I think.
